h1: Corner grinders — weld seam grinding machines for boxes, cabinets, doors and tube frames
intro: A corner grinder (corner sanding machine, weld seam sander) grinds the weld on the corner of a welded box, cabinet, door or tray flush with the sheet, or to a neat radius, ready for paint or polishing — work that takes long minutes with a hand grinder and never looks the same twice. NovoTech sells the corner grinders of Gecam, built in Parma, Italy: the hand-fed 131 and 136, where an abrasive belt on an oscillating fork grinds corners up to 5-7/8″ and 11-13/16″ high to a radius of 3/64″ to 3/8″; the 135, whose head travels the full length of the edge by itself on boxes with edges up to 59″; and PLC-controlled machines for series work — an upper-corner grinder, a six-head grinder and a grinder for the welds of 90° tube frames. Supplied with a CSA-approved panel, installed and supported from Mississauga, ON.

faq.q: What does a corner grinder do?
faq.a: It grinds the weld bead on an outside corner of a welded box, cabinet, door or tray flush with the sheet — or to a radius — so the corner can be painted, powder-coated or polished without visible weld. The belt runs over rollers or a pad shaped for the corner, so the result is the same on every part, unlike hand grinding.

The 131 and 136 are hand-fed: the operator moves the corner along the belt — quick to set up for mixed boxes and doors. The 135 clamps the box and runs the head along the whole edge by itself, which suits long edges and repeat work, and a second head doubles its output. For high volumes of one part, the PLC machines grind two corners or a whole tube-frame corner per cycle.

The oscillating fork of the 131 and 136 grinds a radius from 3/64″ to 3/8″ (R1 – R10 mm), or a sharp corner. The 135 grinds the weld flush; its PLUS version adds vertical, horizontal and oscillating head movement for radiusing.

faq.q: How high a box can it take?
faq.a: Corner height up to 5-7/8″ on the 131 and 7-7/8″ or 11-13/16″ on the 136 (19-11/16″ on request). The 135 is limited by edge length — 31-1/2″ or 59″ — and the six-head grinder takes boxes up to 5-7/8″ high.

faq.q: Can you build a machine for my part?
faq.a: Yes. Gecam designs special corner grinders around the part — the upper-corner, six-head and tube-frame machines on this page are examples. Send us a drawing or photo of the part and the weld, and the number of parts a shift.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.

origin_feature.title: Made in Italy by Gecam
origin_feature.text: Gecam designs and builds deburring, grinding and finishing machines at Vicofertile, Parma — 100 % made in Italy, with components from Italian suppliers within 125 miles (200 km) of the plant. In 2005 it took over Eurofintec, the abrasive-belt machine builder whose name its pipe and belt machines still carry.
